items.text: A material upstream FOSS dependency publishes a new major release. Automation detects it, records release notes/currentness, stages an isolated candidate, runs characterization/contract/migration/target gates, and either adopts/adapts/defers/rejects it without modifying the accepted runtime until promotion.
items.notes: The isolated candidate gate detects newer semantic versions, distinguishes major updates, requires exact source/release identity and an isolated candidate reference, evaluates currentness/license/security/contract/migration/target gates, rejects policy-critical failure, defers unknown or incomplete gates, and never mutates the accepted runtime. The synthetic contract is source/unit qualified; registry detection, a real upstream major candidate, dependency installation, migration/target breadth, promotion, and release evidence remain open.

items.text: A new FOSS entrant appears that provides a currently missing or locally bespoke capability with materially lower lifecycle cost. The ecosystem radar adds it to the Capability Coverage Matrix, performs exact source/license/security/fit evaluation, and either replaces/consolidates the old path after proof or records why not.
items.notes: The shared isolated-candidate owner requires a recorded capability gap, exact source/license/candidate identity, and source/license/security/fit/maintenance/target gates. Policy-critical failure rejects the entrant; incomplete evidence defers it; an all-PASS fixture returns ADOPT_CANDIDATE without replacing the accepted runtime. A real entrant, lifecycle-cost comparison, install/replace proof, and promotion remain open.

items.text: A high-severity vulnerability affects a shipped optional dependency. The security fast lane identifies affected scope, prevents false PASS, qualifies a fix/replacement or safely disables/degrades only the affected capability, and preserves unrelated core operation and user data.
items.notes: The synthetic high-severity fast lane blocks release when no qualified fix or safe disable path exists, returns FIX_CANDIDATE only after source/security/contract/target gates pass, and returns DISABLE_OPTIONAL only when optional isolation, core regression, and data preservation are proven. The result prevents false PASS but does not claim a real advisory, replacement, or runtime disablement; live advisory feeds, dependency isolation, and release qualification remain open.

items.text: An adopted FOSS component is removed from public package/repository infrastructure. The accepted Omnevum release continues to run, and the documented reconstruction path either succeeds from retained lawful inputs or reports the exact bounded reconstruction limitation without silently substituting content.
items.notes: The removal gate continues only when retained lawful inputs reconstruct the path with core/canonical preservation or when an explicit bounded reconstruction limitation is recorded with the same preservation checks; otherwise it blocks release. Synthetic source/unit cases are qualified. Real package/source disappearance, lawful reconstruction assets, and release-profile recovery remain open.

items.text: A copyleft FOSS capability is selected because it materially dominates alternatives. The release proves exact license/provenance/notice/corresponding-source obligations or isolates the component through a compliant integration; no license is silently misrepresented.
items.notes: The copyleft gate requires exact license identity, notice, corresponding-source availability, isolation/compliance evidence, and reviewed legal state before admission; incomplete obligations isolate the candidate and failed isolation rejects it. This is an engineering control contract, not legal advice or a claim that a new copyleft capability was selected.

items.text: An upstream project adds functionality that supersedes an Omnevum local patch or duplicate subsystem. The maintenance cycle proves parity, removes the obsolete local path, reduces the patch/delta burden, and reruns affected regression/release evidence.
items.notes: The parity gate defers stale/unknown evidence, retains a local path after parity/regression failure, adapts when upstream is compatible but local delta remains, and returns REMOVE_LOCAL_PATCH only when parity, migration, regression, and delta-reduction gates pass. No real upstream patch removal occurred; current upstream comparison and release rerun remain open.

items.text: A representative workflow receives a source containing information already needed by three or more modules/views. The user supplies the information once. items.text: A constrained monthly surplus cannot fully fund all active goals. Omnevum detects the shared-resource conflict once, shows the aggregate shortfall and affected goals, and prepares multiple feasible alternatives that preserve user-defined hard constraints. items.text: A candidate intervention has supported positive effects on two goals and a modeled downside on a third domain. Omnevum surfaces both the synergy and conflict, identifies evidence/assumption status for each edge, and preserves the option to take no action. items.text: A dependency graph contains both an accidental cycle and an intentionally modeled feedback loop.
